title: DeepAmbigQA: Ambiguous Multi-hop Questions for Benchmarking LLM Answer Completeness
gist: Apple researchers introduce DEEPAMBIGQA, a 3,600-question benchmark built by an automatic knowledge-graph-grounded pipeline (DEEPAMBIGQAGEN) that combines entity-name ambiguity with multi-hop reasoning; even GPT-5 with search tools scores only 0.13 exact match on ambiguous questions and 0.21 on non-ambiguous ones, exposing answer completeness (not single-fact accuracy) as the unsolved axis of search-augmented QA. The page is a short paper abstract, and the surrounding page also lists two older Apple QA papers on visual-question rewriting and conversational question rewriting, so the record's stated category of on-device AI/vision understates that this is a search-and-knowledge-bases result.

themes.theme: Answer completeness as the unsolved QA axis

insights.claim: LLMs equipped with integrated search tools still fail to produce complete answer sets for complex open-domain questions, making set completeness — not per-fact accuracy — the binding constraint on retrieval-augmented QA quality.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Vendor benchmarks that report single-answer accuracy overstate real agentic-search readiness; watch for completeness/recall metrics before underwriting enterprise RAG deployments.
insights.quote: Large language models (LLMs) with integrated search tools show strong promise in open-domain question answering (QA), yet they often struggle to produce complete answer set to complex questions

insights.claim: On the DEEPAMBIGQA benchmark, state-of-the-art GPT-5 achieves only 0.13 exact match on name-ambiguous questions and 0.21 on non-ambiguous questions, meaning the frontier model fails roughly four out of five multi-hop completeness tasks.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A hard, quantified ceiling on frontier-model deep research: agentic search products promising exhaustive answer sets are shipping against a ~0.13–0.21 EM baseline, which is a durable failure surface competitors and auditors can exploit.
insights.quote: even state-of-the-art GPT-5 show incomplete answers, achieving only 0.13 exact match on ambiguous questions and 0.21 on non-ambiguous questions

insights.claim: Name ambiguity roughly halves frontier-model performance relative to unambiguous multi-hop questions (0.13 versus 0.21 exact match), isolating entity disambiguation as a distinct and larger error source than multi-hop reasoning alone.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Entity resolution and knowledge-graph linking layers — not just bigger context windows — are where incremental spend actually moves QA accuracy; favors vendors with structured-knowledge assets.

insights.claim: The paper frames the failure as two compounding requirements — distinguishing multiple entities sharing the same name and aggregating evidence across a large candidate set — using the example question of which actor from the film Heat won at least one Academy Award.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A cheap reusable diagnostic: probe any deep-research product with same-title/same-name aggregation queries to expose completeness failure in minutes.
insights.quote: “Which actor from the film Heat won at least one Academy Award?”
insights.locator: which requires (1) distinguishing between multiple films

insights.claim: DEEPAMBIGQAGEN is an automatic data generation pipeline that constructs QA tasks from text corpora linked to a knowledge graph, systematically embedding name ambiguity and multi-step reasoning into natural, verifiable questions.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Benchmark supply is becoming programmatic and adversarially targetable, which shortens the shelf life of any leaderboard score and raises the value of proprietary knowledge graphs as evaluation infrastructure.
insights.quote: we introduce DEEPAMBIGQAGEN, an automatic data generation pipeline that constructs QA tasks grounded in text corpora and linked knowledge graph, generating natural and verifiable questions that systematically embed name ambiguity and multi-step reasoning
insights.locator: To address this, we introduce DEEPAMBIGQAGEN

insights.claim: The resulting DEEPAMBIGQA dataset contains 3,600 multi-hop questions with exactly half requiring explicit name-ambiguity resolution, giving a controlled A/B split that isolates the marginal cost of disambiguation.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The 50/50 design makes the benchmark a clean ablation instrument, so expect it to be adopted quickly for competitive model comparisons.
insights.quote: a dataset of 3,600 questions requiring multi-hop reasoning and half of them explicit name ambiguity resolving
insights.locator: Based on this, we build DEEPAMBIGQA

insights.claim: The authors argue existing QA benchmarks rarely evaluate name ambiguity and multi-hop evidence aggregation jointly, implying published QA leaderboards have a structural blind spot rather than merely being saturated.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Treat existing QA leaderboard gains as partly measurement artifact; new benchmark categories reset apparent model rankings.
insights.quote: Existing QA benchmarks rarely evaluate both challenges jointly.

insights.claim: Apple has pursued question disambiguation as a recurring research line since at least 2021, having previously shown conversational QA can be decomposed into a question-rewriting subtask that turns context-dependent ambiguous questions into unambiguous ones.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Signals sustained Apple investment in assistant-grade retrieval and disambiguation rather than a one-off paper, relevant to expectations for Siri/search capabilities.
insights.quote: The question rewriting (QR) subtask is specifically designed to reformulate ambiguous questions, which depend on the conversational context, into unambiguous questions

insights.claim: Apple's 2022 OKVQA work found many visual questions containing deictic referential phrases can be rewritten as non-grounded text questions and answered by existing text-based QA systems, i.e. reusing language infrastructure instead of building dedicated multimodal reasoners.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A cost-avoidance pattern: rewriting multimodal queries into text lets a company amortize one text QA stack across modalities, lowering the compute bill versus training separate vision reasoners.

insights.claim: The DEEPAMBIGQA author list mixes Apple staff with University of California, Santa Barbara affiliates and flags that lead-author work was done while at Apple, indicating the project ran on academic collaboration and that at least one contributor has since departed.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Minor but real AI-talent-flow datapoint: Apple's QA research output is partly intern/academic-driven and subject to attrition, a recurring constraint on its in-house model roadmap.
